problem: Zero-shot LLM/VLM navigation work reports aggregate success but rarely follows a model's local judgments (landmark matching, history use, verification) through actual motion and stopping. It is unclear whether correct understanding turns into sustained progress and appropriate STOP.
motivation: Recognizing an entrance does not mean the agent crosses it, and nearing a goal does not mean it stops properly. The paper evaluates GPT-6-Astra in a complete observation-decision-execution workflow and links its recorded responses to executed actions and outcomes.
key_idea: Evaluate GPT-6-Astra in a zero-shot VLN-CE workflow with externally managed context and action control, and audit its judgments against executed motion and stopping to expose a gap between understanding and autonomous completion.
insight: Local judgments are often supported by the evidence: timing and order checks are supported in 84.9% and 82.0% of clauses, and 48 of 75 verification processes clarify an uncertain judgment. These judgments do not reliably become progress or a proper stop. Only 36.0% of episodes succeed with a workflow-accepted STOP, while another 16.0% meet the distance criterion only at the step limit. The results depend on both model and workflow (context selection, controller); there are no ablations, so causal attribution is not possible.
method: Workflow: an externally managed loop of direct API calls (no agent harness, no fine-tuning). Code selects context, retains records, schedules reviews and constrains execution.
Four prompted roles: task planning, progress assessment, action proposal and arrival assessment, each a separate chat request with a role-specific system prompt.

Context management: up to 4 selected observation frames plus an 8-action receipt window per action call; progress and arrival reviews draw on archive, event records and prior reviews. The model can request saved images.
Action controller: depth and failed-heading restrictions, alignment/recovery actions, and completion checks before accepting STOP. Initial 12-heading panorama, then frontal RGB-D.
Audit protocol: offline, assistant-assisted labels (S/C/U) for grounding, temporal reasoning, action adjustment and verification, checked against images, receipts and GT.

setting.backbone: GPT-6-Astra (frozen, reasoning effort medium, via API)
setting.observation: initial 12-heading panorama, then egocentric frontal RGB-D
setting.action_space: low-level FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN ±15° / STOP, 100-step budget
setting.privileged: none online; GT trajectories and endpoints used only for offline evaluation and audit

numbers.eval_set_note: first 50 episodes (by ID) of the 100-episode Open-Nav pool, 9 scenes
numbers.extra: one run, seed 0; externally managed context and action control; 100-step budget; subset exposed during workflow development; 16.0% of episodes succeed only at budget termination
numbers.evidence: Table 2, last row: GPT-6-Astra + our workflow, 50 of ON-100, Mono., 4.34 / 70.79 / 62.00 / 52.00 / 48.90

results: On 50 R2R-CE val-unseen episodes, the system reaches SR 52.0, SPL 48.9 and nDTW 70.79. That is above the zero-shot AgenticNav-GPT-5.5 on SR by ~-3 (its SR is 55.0, so it is lower on SR) and close on SPL (48.41). Only 18/50 episodes succeed with an accepted STOP, 8 succeed at budget termination, and 3 accepted STOPs fail.
limitations: Small fixed 50-episode prefix, single run, and exposure to the subset during workflow development, so no variance or full-split estimate and no matched comparison with other methods.
No ablations, so model and workflow (context, controller) contributions cannot be separated; audits are assistant-assisted with no human or inter-rater validation.
High inference cost: 9,208 generations, 110M input tokens, and 22.55 hours of cumulative call time on 50 episodes.
